title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
summary: Interleaves reasoning traces with task actions and environment feedback.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
summary: Explores and evaluates multiple intermediate reasoning paths with lookahead and backtracking.

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
summary: LATS combines language-model value estimates and self-reflection with Monte Carlo tree search and environment feedback.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
summary: Trains a model with self-supervised API-call examples to decide when and how to use external tools.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
summary: Introduces ToolLLM and ToolBench, covering tool-use data construction, model training and evaluation over real APIs.

title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
summary: Evaluates simulated user conversations with API tools and policy guidelines by comparing final database state with goal state.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses verbal reflection and an episodic text buffer to improve later trials without updating model weights.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
summary: Uses an automatic curriculum, executable skill library and iterative prompting for open-ended Minecraft exploration, without parameter fine-tuning.

title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
The Landscape of Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Survey
summary: Surveys agentic RL as temporally extended, partially observable interaction, with capability and application taxonomies; arXiv v5 was revised in April 2026.
legacy_note: Broad survey of agentic reinforcement learning

title: From Reasoning to Agentic: Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
summary: Updated v3 surveys 69 papers through July 2026, including 56 core credit-assignment methods, and examines identification limits and evaluation controls for agentic RL.
legacy_note: Token, turn and multi-agent reward attribution

title: Milestone-Guided Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Language Agents
summary: Uses milestone boundaries, segment-level reward shaping and dual-scale advantage estimates for long-horizon agent training.

title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Derives turn-level temporal-difference rewards from frozen-reference answer probabilities at tool-call boundaries, without training a separate critic.

title: Rewarding Beliefs, Not Actions: Consistency-Guided Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: ReBel uses structured beliefs, belief-consistency supervision and belief-aware trajectory grouping for long-horizon agent training.

title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
summary: AgeMem treats storing, retrieving, updating, summarizing and discarding memory as policy actions, trained with progressive RL and step-wise GRPO.
legacy_note: RL for memory read, write, summarize and discard

title: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
summary: MemoryArena evaluates whether agents use earlier interactions and feedback to solve later, interdependent tasks across sessions.

title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
summary: AMA-Bench evaluates memory over long agent-environment trajectories; its authors also propose causality-graph memory retrieval.

title: Mem2ActBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Utilization in Task-Oriented Autonomous Agents
summary: Tests whether agents proactively apply long-term memory to tool selection and parameter grounding in task-oriented interactions.
legacy_note: Long-term memory use in agent actions

title: Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic–Procedural Memory
summary: H-EPM combines episodic summaries with a procedural tool graph and uses successful tool transitions to guide RL exploration.

title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks
summary: SINKFLEX-RL combines a tool-use environment wrapper, rollout dataflow and sink-aware FlexAttention for memory-feasible long-horizon training.

title: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
summary: Introduces episode-level and anchor-state step-level relative advantage estimates for multi-turn agent training.

title: Agent Lightning: Train ANY AI Agents with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Proposes an agent-training interface that separates agent execution from RL training and decomposes trajectories into training transitions.

title: SHADOW: Dynamic-Aware Credit Assignment Against Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: Groups dynamically consistent states and uses a local dynamics-aware advantage estimator for long-horizon agent credit assignment.

title: Intrinsic Credit Assignment for Long Horizon Interaction
summary: ΔBelief-RL rewards changes in an agent’s probability assigned to the target solution, providing intermediate credit for information-seeking actions.

title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL
summary: Lets an agent harness own the interaction loop while RL training observes LLM request-response pairs; studies retokenization, sample merging, advantage and loss normalization.

title: A Survey on the Optimization of Large Language Model-based Agents
summary: Surveys parameter-driven and parameter-free agent optimization, including reinforcement learning, trajectory construction, reward design, prompting, and retrieval.

title: A Survey of Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models: Towards Recursively Self-Improving and Collective Agents
summary: Organizes agentic reasoning into foundational, self-evolving, and collective layers, and distinguishes test-time orchestration from RL and supervised post-training.

title: A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half: Towards Self-Evolving and Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Surveys memory substrates, cognitive mechanisms, and memory subjects; reviews learned memory-operation policies and evaluation of memory utility.

title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Surveys long-horizon agents across planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, and foundations, emphasizing the limits of outcome-only signals.

title: HiPER: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents
summary: Separates high-level subgoal planning from multi-step execution and estimates advantages at both levels.

title: Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: HCAPO uses the LLM as a post-hoc critic to refine step-level Q-values and combines advantages at multiple scales.

title: Memory-R2: Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
summary: Compares local rerollouts from the same intermediate memory state while retaining a global long-horizon objective for memory operations.

title: Learning from Environmental Feedback: Credit Assignment across Multiple Timescales for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: EFCA reweights returns using short-term action feedback and medium-term state history alongside long-term outcomes.

title: Granularity-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: GACA uses a decision criticality score from rollout token log-probabilities to adaptively mix episode- and step-level credit without extra rollouts.

title: Targeting Pivotal Decisions for Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: ProVer selects potentially pivotal segments by comparing successful and failed trajectories, then estimates local advantage from sampled continuations before and after each segment.

title: SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: SHARPO uses teacher-student log-probability gaps to reweight GRPO advantages at environment-facing segment granularity.

title: SCAD: Structured Credit Assignment and Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: SCAD separates planning from bounded subtask execution, combining cross-rollout prefix-tree planning credit with local teacher-guided execution distillation.

title: VETTA: Coordinating Turn- and Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents
summary: VETTA estimates turn- and token-level advantages with two heads on a shared lightweight critic for PPO updates.

title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL
summary: LVRL estimates policy-aware state values with a pretrained LLM, deriving step-level credit from value differences without fitting a separate critic.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
summary: Introduces PPO, an online policy-gradient family that reuses sampled data for multiple minibatch optimization epochs.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
summary: Derives a direct classification objective for preference alignment without online sampling during fine-tuning.

title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model
summary: RAP uses an LLM as both a reasoning agent and an approximate world model, with tree search guiding planning.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
summary: Surveys LLM-based autonomous-agent construction, applications and evaluation; it is background for agent architecture rather than an RL method.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
summary: Introduces DeepSeekMath and Group Relative Policy Optimization for mathematical reasoning.

title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
summary: BudgetMem trains a compact routing policy to choose among memory-processing budget tiers according to the query and cost target.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses reinforcement learning to elicit reasoning patterns on verifiable tasks; background for reasoning RL rather than evidence of external agent interaction.

title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
summary: Introduces DAPO and an open training system for large-scale reasoning-oriented LLM reinforcement learning.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
summary: Introduces virtual context management across memory tiers for document analysis and multi-session chat; it is a memory-system background work.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
summary: Uses knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank for long-term retrieval over accumulated information; not an RL-trained memory policy.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
summary: Iteratively generates, critiques and revises outputs with one LLM, without reinforcement learning or additional training.

title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
summary: Uses external tools to validate and revise an LLM's initial output through iterative critiquing.

title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
summary: Trains a model to propose and solve code-reasoning tasks, using a code executor for verifiable self-play rewards.

title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments
summary: Adapts actor-critic learning to multi-agent settings by accounting for other agents' policies; classical MARL background.

title: Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients
summary: COMA uses a centralized critic and a counterfactual baseline to assign credit to individual agents in cooperative MARL.

title: QMIX: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Combines per-agent values into a monotonic joint action-value for centralized training and decentralized execution.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
summary: Studies PPO-based methods on cooperative multi-agent benchmarks and reports strong performance with modest tuning.

title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
summary: Introduces a simulated shopping website where agents navigate pages and act on product-search instructions.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
summary: Introduces reproducible functional websites and tasks for evaluating web agents' task completion.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
summary: Provides web-instruction tasks and action sequences collected across diverse real websites for generalist web-agent evaluation.

title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
summary: Introduces visually grounded web tasks for evaluating multimodal agents that process image and text inputs.

title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
summary: Curates machine-learning engineering competition tasks to evaluate agents that prepare data, train models and run experiments.

title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
summary: Introduces assistant questions combining reasoning, multimodal handling, web browsing and tool use.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
summary: Introduces software-engineering issues from real GitHub repositories for evaluating repository-level code edits.
